newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Arabs to attend Mideast economic summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Arabs to attend Mideast economic summit.

text.p: In remarks implicitly aimed at Saudi Arabia, the United States on Wednesday called on Arab countries which have threatened to boycott a regional summit in Qatar in November to reconsider their position.

"We encourage all Arab countries to participate in the Doha economic summit," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "Those Arab governments who said they won't attend, we hope they'll reconsider their positions."

The summit, which brings together Arab countries and Israel, has been held annually since 1994 with strong U.S. backing. But this year, many Arab countries are angry at what they see as Israeli stalling on the Middle East peace process.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah said in remarks published on Monday that Saudi Arabia would not attend the Doha gathering and had advised Qatar to cancel it.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday that his country, which hosted the gathering last year, had not yet decided whether it would attend this year.
"If the peace process is to be carried out in all of its dimensions, people have to be willing to go to economic conferences," Burns told a news briefing.

"If that logic was allowed to prevail in the Middle East, that because there are problems you shouldn't move forward in any way with any other aspect of the peace negotiations, we wouldn't have a prayer of moving forward."

Qatar said on Wednesday it was going ahead with preparations for the conference, regardless of pressure from other Arab states to cancel or postpone it. Syria, Lebanon, Iraq and Libya have never attended the gathering.
